instruments.name: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.x

facet_hints.scope: PCI DSS is contractual, not statutory, and applies only where cardholder data is stored, processed or transmitted. Determine scope first: a service that redirects to a hosted payment page has a very different obligation set from one that touches a PAN.
facet_hints.sad: Sensitive authentication data must never be stored after authorisation — CVV, full track data, PIN blocks. This is the check most often failed in code.
facet_hints.pan_storage: Where a PAN is stored it must be rendered unreadable; masking rules apply on display.
facet_hints.requirements: Requirements 3 (protect stored account data), 4 (protect in transit), 6 (secure development), 8 (identify and authenticate), 10 (log and monitor), 11 (test), 12 (policy).

seed_obligations.title: Never store sensitive authentication data after authorisation
testable_as: no CVV/CVC column or field anywhere in the schema
card fields not written to logs

seed_obligations.title: Render the primary account number unreadable wherever it is stored
testable_as: tokenisation or strong cryptography with documented key management

seed_obligations.title: Encrypt cardholder data in transit over open networks
testable_as: no card data in URLs or query strings

seed_obligations.title: Log and monitor access to cardholder data
testable_as: audit log covering access to card data
